rules.weightBasisIBW: Constant: for ANY infusion (or weight-based bolus) whose weightBasis is IBW, the weight used for the per-kg calculation is min(IBW, TBW) — i.e. IBW unless IBW exceeds the patient's actual total body weight, in which case TBW is used instead. Current code (calcSuggestedDose / 'Total will use IBW' hint) does NOT apply this cap yet — falls back to plain ibw ?? tbw. Needs fixing when this library is wired in.
rules.doseCalcRounding: Auto-calculated suggested doses need their OWN rounding granularity (doseCalc.roundTo), separate from the slider's step — confirmed NOT always the same: Propofol rounds to 10 (matches its step=10), but Etomidate rounds to 1 despite a 0.1 step.
rules.doseCalcUnitAgnostic: doseCalc's per-kg multiplier must NOT be hardcoded as 'mgPerKg' — Dexmedetomidine doses in mcg/kg, not mg/kg. Rename to a unit-agnostic field (e.g. perKg, interpreted in the drug's own canonical unit) rather than mgPerKg specifically. Final doseCalc schema: { perKg?: number, flat?: number, basis?: 'IBW'|'TBW', roundTo: number } — interpreted in the drug's own `unit`.
rules.doseCalcPerRoute: Confirmed via Ketamine: when a drug has multiple routes, the per-kg auto-fill multiplier can differ BY ROUTE (Ketamine IV 2mg/kg, IM 4mg/kg, IN 3mg/kg, PO 8mg/kg, all IBW, all roundTo 10). doseCalc therefore needs to be keyed per-route (Record<route, DoseCalc>), not one flat object per drug, whenever routes.length > 1.
rules.doseModeByRoute: Confirmed via Lidocaine: the DOSING MODE itself (not just the doseCalc multiplier) can vary by route. IV = flat mg dose with a stepper. SC / Local infiltration / PD (peridural) / IT (intrathecal) = concentration% + volume(mL) — the same 'pick a concentration, dial a volume' mechanism already built for LA infusions (concentrationOptions), but now ALSO needed at the BOLUS level, keyed per-route. Same applies to infusions: IV infusion = rate in mg/kg/hr; PD/IT infusion = concentration% + rate(mL/hr). One drug, one catalog entry, but routes split into 'dose-mode' routes (flat unit) vs 'concentration-mode' routes (% + volume/rate), each with their own range/step/quickValues. Schema needs: routeMode: Record<route, 'dose'|'concentration'>, plus per-route range/quick/concentrationOptions where mode is 'concentration'.
rules.infusionSuggestedRate: Infusions can have a suggested STARTING rate too (Atracurium: 0.3 mg/kg/hr), same idea as bolus doseCalc but for the infusion's rate field. New field: suggestedRate (interpreted in the infusion's own unit, possibly per-kg if weightBasis is set). Not yet built in the UI (infusion start currently has no auto-fill, only bolus does via calcSuggestedDose) — needs its own wiring.
rules.unitSwitchNoConversion: CONFIRMED BUG-IN-WAITING, not yet fixed: DoseSelector's onUnitChange only relabels the unit (IntraopTimetable.tsx:2735,2765 — setFp(f => ({...f, unit: u})) / rateUnit), it does NOT convert the numeric value. Decision: until a real conversion-on-switch feature is built, every drug gets exactly ONE canonical unit (no multi-unit allowedUnits with incompatible bases like mg/kg/hr vs mcg/kg/min). Revisit as its own feature later if dual-unit entry is wanted.
rules.variableStep: Confirmed via Bupivacaine: dose/volume sliders sometimes need a non-uniform step (fine below a threshold, coarser above) — same idea as mobile's existing weight wheel (0.5kg steps up to 20kg, then whole-kg after). New field: variableStep?: { upTo: number, step: number }[] (ordered ascending by upTo, last entry's step applies above its upTo). When present, overrides the flat `step` field for slider behavior.
rules.canonicalUnitsExtended: Original canonical infusion-unit list (IU/kg/hr, IU/hr, mL/hr, mcg/kg/min, mg/kg/hr, g/kg/hr) was missing several units actually needed clinically. Full audited list of infusion units in use as of this pass: IU/min (Vasopressin), g/hr (Magnesium sulfate), mL/hr (Lidocaine PD/IT, concentration-rate mode), mcg/kg/hr (Dexmedetomidine, Fentanyl, Sufentanil), mcg/kg/min (Remifentanil, Alfentanil, Cisatracurium-equivalent before conversion, Atracurium-equivalent, Mivacurium, Dobutamine, Milrinone, Levosimendan, Dopamine), mcg/min (Isoproterenol), mg/hr (Metaraminol), mg/kg/hr (Propofol, Ketamine, Esketamine, Rocuronium, Vecuronium, Cisatracurium, Atracurium, Lidocaine IV), ng/kg/min (Angiotensin II). Final canonical infusion-unit list: IU/kg/hr, IU/hr, IU/min, mL/hr, ng/kg/min, mcg/min, mcg/kg/min, mcg/kg/hr, mg/min, mg/hr, mg/kg/hr, g/hr, g/kg/hr. Always check this list before introducing a new infusion unit — extend deliberately, don't invent ad hoc.
rules.prepStrengthInfusion: New mechanism activated via Amiodarone: when an infusion is dosed in mL/hr with a FIXED single prep strength (not a multi-choice % list like LA concentrationOptions), record prepStrength: { mg: number, mL: number } on the infusion profile. Total mg delivered = rate(mL/hr) * (prepStrength.mg/prepStrength.mL) * hours. UI needs to prompt for this once per drug (or let the user override per-case if their pharmacy mixes differently) — not yet wired into the dose-selector UI.
rules.doseCalcCap: doseCalc needs an optional cap field — PCC 4-factor: 25 IU/kg, but the computed auto-fill must never exceed 3000 IU regardless of weight (heavy patients would otherwise compute beyond the safe ceiling). Schema: doseCalc.cap?: number — clamp the computed suggestion to this value before applying roundTo.
